sanskrit: mārīca śrūyatāṃ tāta vacanaṃ mama bhāṣataḥ ārto 'smi mama cārtasya bhavān hi paramā gatiḥ
english: "O Mārīca, dear one, hear the words I now speak to you. I am in distress, and for me in distress you are indeed the highest refuge."

sanskrit: jānīṣe tvaṃ janasthānaṃ bhrātā yatra kharo mama dūṣaṇaś ca mahābāhuḥ svasā śūrpaṇakhā ca me
english: "You know Janasthāna, where my brother Khara dwells, and the mighty-armed Dūṣaṇa, and my sister Śūrpaṇakhā as well."

sanskrit: triśirāś ca mahātejā rākṣasaḥ piśitāśanaḥ anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā labdhalakṣā niśācarāḥ
english: "And the greatly resplendent flesh-eating rākṣasa Triśiras, and many other valiant night-roving rākṣasas of unerring aim."

sanskrit: vasanti manniyogena adhivāsaṃ ca rākṣasaḥ bādhamānā mahāraṇye munīn ye dharmacāriṇaḥ
english: "Those rākṣasas dwell there under my command and as my appointed garrison, oppressing in that great forest the sages who walk in righteousness."

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām śūrāṇāṃ labdhalakṣāṇāṃ kharacittānuvartinām
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds, valiant and unerring in aim, following the will of Khara —"

sanskrit: te tv idānīṃ janasthāne vasamānā mahābalāḥ saṃgatāḥ param āyattā rāmeṇa saha saṃyuge
english: "— those great-powered ones now dwelling in Janasthāna met in total dependence upon one another in battle with Rāma."

sanskrit: tena saṃjātaroṣeṇa rāmeṇa raṇamūrdhani anuktvā paruṣaṃ kiṃ cic charair vyāpāritaṃ dhanuḥ
english: "By that Rāma, inflamed with wrath, without speaking a single harsh word, his bow was set to work with arrows at the forefront of battle."

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām nihatāni śarais tīkṣṇair mānuṣeṇa padātinā
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain with sharp arrows by that human fighting on foot."

sanskrit: kharaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇaś ca nipātitaḥ hatvā triśirasaṃ cāpi nirbhayā daṇḍakāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: "Khara was slain in battle and Dūṣaṇa was felled; having also killed Triśiras, he made the Daṇḍaka forest free from fear."

sanskrit: pitrā nirastaḥ kruddhena sabhāryaḥ kṣīṇajīvitaḥ sa hantā tasya sainyasya rāmaḥ kṣatriyapāṃsanaḥ
english: "This Rāma, disgrace of the kṣatriyas, banished by his angry father along with his wife as one whose life-force is spent — he is the slayer of that army."

sanskrit: aśīlaḥ karkaśas tīkṣṇo mūrkho lubdho 'jitendriyaḥ tyaktadharmas tv adharmātmā bhūtānām ahite rataḥ
english: "He is without virtue, harsh, cruel, foolish, greedy, with unmastered senses, one who has abandoned dharma — a soul of adharma, devoted to the harm of all beings."

sanskrit: yena vairaṃ vināraṇye sattvam āśritya kevalam karṇanāsāpahāreṇa bhaginī me virūpitā
english: "By him, without cause in the forest, relying solely on his own courage, my sister was disfigured by the cutting off of her ears and nose."

sanskrit: tasya bhāryāṃ janasthānāt sītāṃ surasutopamām ānayiṣyāmi vikramya sahāyas tatra me bhava
english: "His wife Sītā, who resembles the daughter of a god, I shall carry away by force from Janasthāna. Be my helper in this."

sanskrit: tvayā hy ahaṃ sahāyena pārśvasthena mahābala bhrātṛbhiś ca surān yuddhe samagrān nābhicintaye
english: "With you, O great-powered one, standing at my side as my helper, and with my brothers, I do not give thought even to all the gods in battle."

sanskrit: tat sahāyo bhava tvaṃ me samartho hy asi rākṣasa vīrye yuddhe ca darpe ca na hy asti sadṛśas tava
english: "Therefore be my helper — you are capable, O rākṣasa; in valour, in battle, and in pride there is none equal to you."

sanskrit: etadartham ahaṃ prāptas tvatsamīpaṃ niśācara śṛṇu tat karma sāhāyye yat kāryaṃ vacanān mama
english: "For this purpose I have come to your presence, O night-rover. Hear the act of assistance to be performed at my word."

sanskrit: sauvarṇas tvaṃ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ āśrame tasya rāmasya sītāyāḥ pramukhe cara
english: "Becoming a golden deer dappled with silver spots, roam before Sītā at the hermitage of that Rāma."

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu niḥsaṃśayaṃ sītā dṛṣṭvā tu mṛgarūpiṇam gṛhyatām iti bhartāraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ cābhidhāsyati
english: "Sītā, upon seeing you in the form of a deer, will without doubt urge her husband and Lakṣmaṇa saying: 'Catch it!'"

sanskrit: tatas tayor apāye tu śūnye sītāṃ yathāsukham nirābādho hariṣyāmi rāhuś candraprabhām iva
english: "Then, once those two have gone away and the place is empty, I shall carry off Sītā at my ease without hindrance, as Rāhu seizes the moon's radiance."

sanskrit: tataḥ paścāt sukhaṃ rāme bhāryāharaṇakarśite visrabdhaṃ prahariṣyāmi kṛtārthenāntarātmanā
english: "Afterwards, when Rāma is wasted by the abduction of his wife, I shall strike him at ease, assured and satisfied in my inmost heart."

sanskrit: tasya rāvaṇakathāṃ śrutvā mārīcasya mahātmanaḥ śuṣkaṃ samabhavad vaktraṃ paritrasto babhūva ca
english: Upon hearing Rāvaṇa's words, the great-souled Mārīca's mouth became dry and he was seized with terror.

sanskrit: sa rāvaṇaṃ trastaviṣaṇṇacetā mahāvane rāmaparākramajñaḥ kṛtāñjalis tattvam uvāca vākyaṃ hitaṃ ca tasmai hitam ātmanaś ca
english: He, with mind terrified and downcast, knowing the might of Rāma, addressed Rāvaṇa in that great forest with joined palms, speaking words that were truthful and salutary both for him and for himself.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rākṣasendrasya vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ pratyuvāca mahāprājño mārīco rākṣaseśvaram
english: Having heard the words of the lord of rākṣasas, the highly wise Mārīca, skilled in speech, replied to the lord of rākṣasas:

sanskrit: sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājan satataṃ priyavādinaḥ apriyasya ca pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
english: "Men who ever speak pleasing words, O king, are easily found; but one who speaks and one who hears what is unpleasant yet salutary — both are rare."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ budhyase rāmaṃ mahāvīryaṃ guṇonnatam ayuktacāraś capalo mahendravaruṇopamam
english: "Surely you do not perceive Rāma — of great valour and exalted in virtues, comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa — for you are of wayward conduct and restless mind."

sanskrit: api svasti bhavet tāta sarveṣāṃ bhuvi rakṣasām api rāmo na saṃkruddhaḥ kuryāl lokam arākṣasaṃ
english: "I hope, dear one, that all the rākṣasas on earth may be well; I hope that Rāma, when angered, may not make the world free of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: api te jīvitāntāya notpannā janakātmajā api sītā nimittaṃ ca na bhaved vyasanaṃ mahat
english: "I hope that the daughter of Janaka has not arisen to be the end of your life; I hope that Sītā may not become the cause of a great calamity."

sanskrit: api tvām īśvaraṃ prāpya kāmavṛttaṃ niraṅkuśam na vinaśyet purī laṅkā tvayā saha sarākṣasā
english: "I hope that the city of Laṅkā, having obtained you as its lord — unrestrained and acting on desire — may not perish along with all its rākṣasas and with you."

sanskrit: tvadvidhaḥ kāmavṛtto hi duḥśīlaḥ pāpamantritaḥ ātmānaṃ svajanaṃ rāṣṭraṃ sa rājā hanti durmatiḥ
english: "For a king of your kind — acting on desire, of evil character, taking wicked counsel — that foolish one destroys himself, his own people, and his kingdom."

sanskrit: na ca pitrā parityakto nāmaryādaḥ kathaṃ cana na lubdho na ca duḥśīlo na ca kṣatriyapāṃsanaḥ
english: "Rāma was not abandoned by his father, nor is he in any way transgressor of decorum; he is not greedy, nor of evil character, nor a disgrace to the kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: na ca dharmaguṇair hīnaiḥ kausalyānandavardhanaḥ na ca tīkṣṇo hi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca hite rataḥ
english: "The increaser of Kausalyā's joy is not devoid of the virtues of dharma; he is not cruel — indeed he is devoted to the welfare of all beings."

sanskrit: vañcitaṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikeyyā satyavādinam kariṣyāmīti dharmātmā tataḥ pravrajito vanam
english: "Seeing his father, a man of truthful speech, deceived by Kaikeyī, the dharma-souled one said 'I shall do it,' and thereupon went forth to the forest."

sanskrit: kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmārthaṃ pitur daśarathasya ca hitvā rājyaṃ ca bhogāṃś ca praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
english: "For the sake of Kaikeyī's desired happiness and his father Daśaratha's, he abandoned his kingdom and pleasures and entered the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: na rāmaḥ karkaśas tāta nāvidvān nājitendriyaḥ anṛtaṃ na śrutaṃ caiva naiva tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "Rāma is not harsh, dear one, nor ignorant, nor of unmastered senses; what is untrue has never been heard of him — you ought not speak so."

sanskrit: rāmo vigrahavān dharmaḥ sādhuḥ satyaparākramaḥ rājā sarvasya lokasya devānām iva vāsavaḥ
english: "Rāma is dharma embodied, a righteous man of true valour, king of all the world as Vāsava is king of the gods."

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvaṃ tasya vaidehīṃ rakṣitāṃ svena tejasā icchasi prasabhaṃ hartuṃ prabhām iva vivasvataḥ
english: "How do you wish to forcibly carry away his Vaidehī, protected by his own blazing energy, as though stealing the radiance of the sun?"

sanskrit: śarārciṣam anādhṛṣyaṃ cāpakhaḍgendhanaṃ raṇe rāmāgniṃ sahasā dīptaṃ na praveṣṭuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "You ought not rashly enter that Rāma-fire blazing in battle, unapproachable, fed by bow and sword, with arrows as its flames."

sanskrit: dhanurvyāditadīptāsyaṃ śarārciṣam amarṣaṇam cāpabāṇadharaṃ vīraṃ śatrusenāpahāriṇam
english: "That hero, bearing bow and arrows, whose blazing mouth is spread wide with his bow, whose flames are arrows, intolerant, the destroyer of enemy armies —"

sanskrit: rājyaṃ sukhaṃ ca saṃtyajya jīvitaṃ ceṣṭam ātmanaḥ nātyāsādayituṃ tāta rāmāntakam ihārhasi
english: "— having abandoned kingdom, ease, and your own dear life, you ought not, dear one, rush up to Rāma here, who is the very end of you."

sanskrit: aprameyaṃ hi tat tejo yasya sā janakātmajā na tvaṃ samarthas tāṃ hartuṃ rāmacāpāśrayāṃ vane
english: "Immeasurable is the blazing energy of him whose Janakātmajā she is; you are not able to carry her away in the forest, for she takes refuge in Rāma's bow."

sanskrit: prāṇebhyo 'pi priyatarā bhāryā nityam anuvratā dīptasyeva hutāśasya śikhā sītā sumadhyamā
english: "The slender-waisted Sītā, ever devoted, more dear to him than his own life, is like the flame of a blazing sacrificial fire — to touch her is to be consumed."

sanskrit: kim udyamaṃ vyartham imaṃ kṛtvā te rākṣasādhipa dṛṣṭaś cet tvaṃ raṇe tena tad antaṃ tava jīvitam jīvitaṃ ca sukhaṃ caiva rājyaṃ caiva sudurlabham
english: "Why undertake this futile effort, O lord of rākṣasas? Should you be seen by him in battle, that is the end of your life — your life, your happiness, and your kingdom, all so difficult to obtain."

sanskrit: sa sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ vibhīṣaṇapuraskṛtaiḥ mantrayitvā tu dharmiṣṭhaiḥ kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ
english: "Together with all your ministers, with the righteous Vibhīṣaṇa placed foremost among them, having deliberated and resolved upon your own course of action —"

sanskrit: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca saṃpradhārya balābalam ātmanaś ca balaṃ jñātvā rāghavasya ca tattvataḥ hitaṃ hi tava niścitya kṣamaṃ tvaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "— having weighed well the strengths and weaknesses of faults and virtues, and knowing truly your own strength and that of Rāghava, you ought to determine what is beneficial for you and act accordingly."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu manye tava na kṣamaṃ raṇe samāgamaṃ kosalarājasūnunā idaṃ hi bhūyaḥ śṛṇu vākyam uttamaṃ kṣamaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca niśācarādhipa
english: "But I think it is not fitting for you to meet the son of the king of Kosala in battle. Hear again this excellent, fitting, and appropriate word, O lord of night-rovers."

sanskrit: kadā cid apy ahaṃ vīryāt paryaṭan pṛthivīm imām balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayan parvatopamaḥ
english: "Once upon a time, roaming this earth out of my own valour, bearing the strength of a thousand elephants, mountain-like in form —"

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśas taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ bhayaṃ lokasya janayan kirīṭī parighāyudhaḥ vyacaraṃ daṇḍakāraṇyam ṛṣimāṃsāni bhakṣayan
english: "— dark as a rain-cloud, with earrings of refined gold, causing fear to the world, crowned, armed with a club, I roamed the Daṇḍaka forest eating the flesh of sages."

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'tha dharmātmā madvitrasto mahāmuniḥ svayaṃ gatvā daśarathaṃ narendram idam abravīt
english: "Then the great sage Viśvāmitra, dharma-souled and terrified of me, went himself to Daśaratha, lord of men, and said this:"

sanskrit: ayaṃ rakṣatu māṃ rāmaḥ parvakāle samāhitaḥ mārīcān me bhayaṃ ghoraṃ samutpannaṃ nareśvara
english: "'Let this Rāma, with concentrated mind, protect me during the ritual observance period; a terrible fear from Mārīca has arisen for me, O lord of men.'"

sanskrit: ity evam ukto dharmātmā rājā daśarathas tadā pratyuvāca mahābhāgaṃ viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim
english: "Thus addressed, the dharma-souled king Daśaratha at that time replied to the greatly blessed great sage Viśvāmitra:"

sanskrit: ūna ṣoḍaśa varṣo 'yam akṛtāstraś ca rāghavaḥ kāmaṃ tu mama yat sainyaṃ mayā saha gamiṣyati badhiṣyāmi muniśreṣṭha śatruṃ tava yathepsitam
english: "'This Rāghava is not yet sixteen years old and has not mastered weapons; but whatever army of mine will march with me — I shall slay your enemy, O best of sages, as you desire.'"

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ sa munī rājānaṃ punar abravīt rāmān nānyad balaṃ loke paryāptaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: "Thus addressed, the sage replied again to the king: 'Other than Rāma, no force in the world is sufficient against that rākṣasa.'"

sanskrit: bālo 'py eṣa mahātejāḥ samarthas tasya nigrahe gamiṣye rāmam ādāya svasti te 'stu paraṃtapaḥ
english: "'Even though a boy, this one of great blazing energy is capable of subduing him. I shall go taking Rāma — may you be well, O scorcher of foes.'"

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā sa munis tam ādāya nṛpātmajam jagāma paramaprīto viśvāmitraḥ svam āśramam
english: "Having spoken thus, the sage Viśvāmitra, exceedingly pleased, took that son of the king and went to his own hermitage."

sanskrit: taṃ tadā daṇḍakāraṇye yajñam uddiśya dīkṣitam babhūvāvasthito rāmaś citraṃ visphārayan dhanuḥ
english: "Then Rāma, consecrated for the sacrifice in the Daṇḍaka forest, stood there wondrously bending his bow."

sanskrit: ajātavyañjanaḥ śrīmān bālaḥ śyāmaḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ ekavastradharo dhanvī śikhī kanakamālayā
english: "A beautiful youth whose secondary marks had not yet appeared, dark-complexioned, of auspicious eyes, wearing a single garment, bearing his bow, with a topknot adorned by a golden garland —"

sanskrit: śobhayan daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ dīptena svena tejasā adṛśyata tadā rāmo bālacandra ivoditaḥ
english: "— illuminating the Daṇḍaka forest with his own blazing energy, Rāma appeared at that time like a new moon rising."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ meghasaṃkāśas taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ balī dattavaro darpād ājagāma tadāśramam
english: "Then I, resembling a rain-cloud, with earrings of refined gold, powerful, having obtained a boon, came to that hermitage out of pride."

sanskrit: tena dṛṣṭaḥ praviṣṭo 'haṃ sahasaivodyatāyudhaḥ māṃ tu dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥ sajyam asaṃbhrāntaś cakāra ha
english: "Seen by him as I entered, he instantly raised his weapon. But upon seeing me, without any agitation, he strung his bow."

sanskrit: avajānann ahaṃ mohād bālo 'yam iti rāghavam viśvāmitrasya tāṃ vedim adhyadhāvaṃ kṛtatvaraḥ
english: "Despising Rāghava out of delusion — thinking 'this is just a boy' — I rushed with great haste toward Viśvāmitra's sacrificial altar."

sanskrit: tena muktas tato bāṇaḥ śitaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ tenāhaṃ tāḍitaḥ kṣiptaḥ samudre śatayojane
english: "Then a sharp arrow was released by him, the destroyer of enemies; struck by it, I was hurled into the sea a hundred yojanas away."

sanskrit: rāmasya śaravegena nirasto bhrāntacetanaḥ pātito 'haṃ tadā tena gambhīre sāgarāmbhasi prāpya saṃjñāṃ cirāt tāta laṅkāṃ prati gataḥ purīm
english: "Driven away by the velocity of Rāma's arrow, my wits reeling, I was cast down by him into the deep ocean waters. After a long time regaining my senses, dear one, I made my way back to the city of Laṅkā."

sanskrit: evam asmi tadā muktaḥ sahāyās te nipātitāḥ akṛtāstreṇa rāmeṇa bālenākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "Thus was I merely released at that time, while your helpers were slain — by that Rāma who had not yet mastered all weapons, a boy of effortless deeds."

sanskrit: tan mayā vāryamāṇas tvaṃ yadi rāmeṇa vigraham kariṣyasy āpadaṃ ghorāṃ kṣipraṃ prāpya naśiṣyasi
english: "Therefore, if you, though warned by me, enter into conflict with Rāma, you will swiftly meet a terrible calamity and perish."

sanskrit: krīḍā ratividhijñānāṃ samājotsavaśālinām rakṣasāṃ caiva saṃtāpam anarthaṃ cāhariṣyasi
english: "You will bring grief and calamity upon the rākṣasas who delight in sport and the arts of pleasure, who are distinguished by their gatherings and festivals."

sanskrit: harmyaprāsādasaṃbādhāṃ nānāratnavibhūṣitām drakṣyasi tvaṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ vinaṣṭāṃ maithilīkṛte
english: "You will see the city of Laṅkā, crowded with mansions and palaces, adorned with jewels of every kind, ruined on account of the Maithilī."

sanskrit: akurvanto 'pi pāpāni śucayaḥ pāpasaṃśrayāt parapāpair vinaśyanti matsyā nāgahrade yathā
english: "Even those who do no evil themselves, innocent ones, are destroyed by another's sin through association with sin — as fish perish in a lake infested with a serpent."

sanskrit: divyacandanadigdhāṅgān divyābharaṇabhūṣitān drakṣyasy abhihatān bhūmau tava doṣāt tu rākṣasān
english: "You will see rākṣasas whose bodies are anointed with divine sandal-paste and adorned with divine ornaments, struck down upon the ground — through your fault."

sanskrit: hṛtadārān sadārāṃś ca daśavidravato diśaḥ hataśeṣān aśaraṇān drakṣyasi tvaṃ niśācarān
english: "You will see night-rovers fleeing in all ten directions, their wives stolen, with wives, survivors of slaughter, shelterless."

sanskrit: śarajālaparikṣiptām agnijvālāsamāvṛtām pradagdhabhavanāṃ laṅkāṃ drakṣyasi tvam asaṃśayam
english: "You will see Laṅkā — surrounded by a net of arrows, enveloped in tongues of fire, its dwellings burnt to ash — this is without doubt."

sanskrit: pramadānāṃ sahasrāṇi tava rājan parigrahaḥ bhava svadāranirataḥ svakulaṃ rakṣarākṣasa
english: "Thousands of women are your household, O king. Be devoted to your own wives; protect your own lineage, O rākṣasa."

sanskrit: mānaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca rājyaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ceṣṭam ātmanaḥ yadīcchasi ciraṃ bhoktuṃ mā kṛthā rāma vipriyam
english: "Honour, prosperity, kingdom, and your own dear life — if you wish to enjoy these long, do not do what is displeasing to Rāma."

sanskrit: nivāryamāṇaḥ suhṛdā mayā bhṛśaṃ prasahya sītāṃ yadi dharṣayiṣyasi gamiṣyasi kṣīṇabalaḥ sabāndhavo yamakṣayaṃ rāmaśarāttajīvitaḥ
english: "If, though earnestly restrained by me your friend, you persist by force and violate Sītā, you will go — with your strength exhausted, your life taken by Rāma's arrow, together with your kinsmen — to the realm of Yama."
